mainTopic: Clashing expressions in a sale or rental: שמואל treats them as a doubt decided by possession, while רב follows the last expression (תפוס לשון אחרון).
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining שמואל. He was only reporting בן ננס's view, and he does not agree with it. For שמואל, two clashing expressions create a doubt. In both the leap-month rental case and the case of the כור sold 'a סלע per סאה', the side already holding the money or grain keeps it. Then רב הונא reports a ruling from בית רב: when a price is said two ways ('an איסתרא, a hundred מעה'), we go by the one said last. The גמרא asks what is new here, since רב already followed the last expression in the leap-month rental case. It answers that both rulings are needed. In the איסתרא case the second phrase looks like a change of mind. In the rental case the second phrase could look like a mere explanation of the first, and רב teaches that we follow the last phrase even there.

steps.title: שמואל does not follow בן ננס; possession is what decides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads שמואל's word 'זו' as 'this is the view of בן ננס', a view he does not hold. In both cases the outcome comes from who is in possession, not from going by the last expression.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, שמואל really meant 'this is the view of בן ננס', but he does not agree with him. Then why does he rule as he does in the leap-month case? Because the winning side is already holding the money. Here too, the buyer is already holding what was measured out to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the earlier problem with שמואל by changing how we read him. He was only reporting בן ננס's view, and he does not agree with it himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier it looked as if שמואל held תפוס לשון אחרון ('go by the last expression'). Now we say he agrees with the חכמים that two clashing expressions create a doubt. In a doubt, money stays with whoever holds it (מוחזק). So in the leap-month case the side holding the rent keeps it, and in the grain case the buyer keeps each סאה already measured to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (used to bring in the true reading)
He does not hold that view
He is holding it, in possession

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל and the side holding the money win here because of possession in a case of doubt, not because the last words of the deal count more.
steps.whatToRemember: For שמואל, clashing expressions make a doubt, and in a doubt the one holding the money or goods keeps it.

phrases.english: Rather, actually, "this" [is the view of בן ננס] —
and he does not hold like him.
And there, what is the reason?
phrases.notes: 'There' means the rental case where the year turned out to have an extra month.

phrases.english: Here too, he is in possession.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the case of the כור sold for thirty סלע, a סלע per סאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction in שמואל's views from the previous section of the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the statement: שמואל was reporting בן ננס's view, which he rejects. The outcomes come from possession in a case of doubt.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל holds תפוס לשון אחרון, which clashes with his other ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל holds clashing expressions create a doubt, and possession decides both cases.

steps.title: A price said two ways: go by the second
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא reports from בית רב: if a seller says 'an איסתרא, a hundred מעה', the price is a hundred מעה. If he says 'a hundred מעה, an איסתרא', the price is an איסתרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said that in the school of רב they say: if the seller said 'an איסתרא, a hundred מעה', it is a hundred מעה. If he said 'a hundred מעה, an איסתרא', it is an איסתרא.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling on a related topic. When a price is named in two ways that don't quite match, we follow whichever one was said last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An איסתרא is worth slightly less than a hundred מעה, so the two prices are not the same. בית רב rules that the later wording decides. This is the rule of תפוס לשון אחרון.

keyTerms.meaning: They say in the school of רב
A silver coin, a little less than a hundred מעה

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, אָמְרִי בֵּי רַב:
phrases.english: רב הונא said: they say in the school of רב:

phrases.notes: The seller names his price twice in a row, and the two amounts are slightly different.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, אָמְרִי בֵּי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new ruling on the same topic of clashing expressions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a price is stated in two different ways, the later wording decides.

steps.title: What is new? רב already taught this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what this ruling adds, since רב already showed he holds תפוס לשון אחרון in the leap-month rental case.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this teaching us? That we go by the last expression? רב already said that once! As רב said: had I been there, I would have given the whole extra month's rent to the landlord.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's report as repeating something רב already said. It proves this by quoting רב's ruling on the extra month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the rental case the deal ended with 'a gold דינר per month'. רב would give the extra month's rent to the landlord, which shows he follows the last expression. So the איסתרא ruling seems to add nothing new, and the גמרא will need to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (what is new here?)
The landlord, the one renting out

steps.confusionAlert: This is רב's own view, the opposite of שמואל's in step 1. רב goes by the last words. שמואל treats clashing words as a doubt.

phrases.english: That we hold onto the last expression?
But רב already said it once!

phrases.notes: He means: if I had been the judge in the case of the year with an extra month.

phrases.english: I would have given all of it to the landlord!
phrases.notes: All of it is the whole extra month's rent. The deal ended with 'a gold דינר per month', so the landlord gets paid for that month too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 2 as adding nothing new.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling from בית רב reported by רב הונא about the איסתרא and the hundred מעה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב already showed in the leap-month rental case that he follows the last expression, so this ruling seems to repeat it.

steps.title: Both rulings are needed because each case could be read differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the איסתרא ruling alone would not teach the leap-month case. In the איסתרא case, the second phrase looks like the seller changing his mind. In the leap-month case, the second phrase could look like he is just explaining the first, so רב had to teach that we still follow the last phrase.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had the איסתרא ruling and not the leap-month ruling, I would have thought: the seller is changing his mind, so of course we follow his last words. But here, in the leap-month case, you might have thought he is only explaining what he meant at first. So רב teaches us that even there we follow the last words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 3 by showing that the איסתרא ruling and the leap-month ruling each teach something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the איסתרא case the two prices clash, so the second phrase reads like a retraction, and following it is easy to understand. In the leap-month rental, the second phrase (a דינר a month) could be read as simply explaining the first (twelve a year), which would mean following the first phrase. רב's leap-month ruling teaches that תפוס לשון אחרון applies even there.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)
He is taking back his first words
He is explaining his first words

steps.whatToRemember: תפוס לשון אחרון applies in two situations. It applies when the second phrase is a change of mind (איסתרא). It also applies when the second phrase could pass as an explanation of the first (leap-month rental).
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up which הָא is which. The first one is the איסתרא case from step 2. The word הָכָא, "here", points to the leap-month rental case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer shows that the rule of following the last phrase does not depend on the speaker clearly changing his mind. That makes the rule much broader.

phrases.notes: "This" is the איסתרא ruling from step 2.

phrases.english: and that had not been stated,
he is retracting his first statement.
that he is explaining his first statement;

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אִיתְּמַר הָא וְלָא אִיתְּמַר הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 3 with a צריכותא: it shows that the איסתרא ruling does not make רב's leap-month ruling unnecessary, so both rulings are needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each ruling is needed because neither one can be learned from the other.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the איסתרא case alone, one would think the last phrase counts only because the seller clearly changed his mind. In the leap-month case, one might then follow the first phrase and treat the second as an explanation.
steps.terutzMaskana: We follow the last phrase both when it is a retraction and when it could pass as an explanation. Each of רב's rulings is needed.
